## What this is

NoteDown is a cross-platform notes app for Android, iOS and the web, in
which every note is a Markdown section and at the same time a to-do.
Functional scope and operating concept (Bedienkonzept) are worked out in
`docs/` and in a clickable **prototype** in `app/` — a real web app,
built like the later app would be, but without a build step, so it can
be opened and tested right away. The technology is decided (see
"Technology direction"): `app/` grows into the real app, wrapped for
Android in `mobile/`, with the sync server in `server/`. The first
milestone is sync between the user's own devices on Android and the web;
the live test setup is described in `docs/operations.md`.

## Device tiers

Every view is designed and checked in these three tiers. The numbers are
the viewports `scripts/screenshot.js --device` uses; the app switches
layout at the CSS widths.

| Tier | Viewport (CSS px) | Input | App layout |
|---|---|---|---|
| desktop | 1440×900 | mouse + hardware keyboard | ≥ 1024 px |
| tablet | 820×1180 portrait | touch only + on-screen keyboard | 600–1023 px |
| phone | 390×844 | touch only + on-screen keyboard | < 600 px |

How a view adapts between the tiers is part of each decision; the rules
that hold for all views are in `docs/interaction-concept.md`.

## Prototype

### Running it

ES modules don't load from `file://`, so the prototype is served from
the repo root — no install, no build:

```bash
python3 scripts/serve.py         # port 8000; or: python3 scripts/serve.py 8080
```

It prints the addresses to open: `http://localhost:8000/app/` on this
computer and `http://<computer-ip>:8000/app/` for a phone or tablet in
the same network. Any other static file server from the repo root works
too (e.g. `python3 -m http.server 8000`).
The prototype holds real notes: the first start shows only the welcome
notes (`app/welcome.md`); `?sample` replaces whatever is stored with the
sample notes, for screenshots and demos.

**Dictation needs a secure context** (https or `localhost`): over
`http://<computer-ip>` the browser blocks the microphone. To try it on
a phone, either add the address under Chrome's
`chrome://flags/#unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure`, or open the
prototype with `?dictation=demo`, which replays
`app/sample/dictation.md` instead of listening.

| Path | Content |

| `app/decor/` | The note motifs' drawings and patterns (`docs/requirements.md` → "Note colors and motifs"), used as CSS masks in the note's tone; generated by `scripts/make-decor.js` |
| `app/icons/` | The app icon: `icon.svg` is the source (Android adaptive-icon grid); `favicon.svg` and the PNGs are generated from it by `scripts/make-icons.js`, like the Android icons in `mobile/android/…/res/mipmap-*` and the reminders' status-bar icon `drawable-*/ic_stat_notedown.png` |
| `app/manifest.webmanifest` | Web app manifest: name, icons, colors for "add to home screen" |
| `app/css/catppuccin.css` | The four Catppuccin flavors as `--ctp-*` variables (generated from `@catppuccin/palette`, don't edit) |
| `app/css/app.css` | All styles; colors only via the semantic tokens at its top |
| `app/js/core/` | Framework-free logic: file format (`notes-file.js`), Markdown helpers — rendering, sections, task states (`markdown.js`), view queries — filter, sort (also the custom order), table of contents, permanent first, which notes each view shows and when trashed ones expire (`query.js`), editing commands (`md-commands.js`), counters — finding them, numbers, times and hours, a step, code of two identities, on WebCrypto plus ML-KEM-768 from `app/vendor/mlkem.js` for the post-quantum hybrid key wrapping (`crypto.js`), the sync client's small decisions — device rows, which keys to wrap, the welcome notes and dropping untouched ones, the blocked message and the notes a device keeps once its identity is deleted (`sync-state.js`), the due-date reminders' schedule and text (`reminders.js`), the export — Markdown with contents and markers, file names, the ZIP (`export.js`), the news feed as read-only notes with their seen / closed / deleted state (`news.js`), labels — the #hashtags of a body, their counts, names from other apps as labels (`labels.js`), reading ZIP archives (`zip.js`) and Google Keep notes as NoteDown notes (`keep-import.js`), restoring and comparing states of the version history (`history.js`), external content — the links & media setting per circle, which addresses load, video or image, the address with its host apart (`external.js`), the open-source license list from the pinned versions (`licenses.js`), the encrypted local vault's records and moving plain data of older versions into it (`vault.js`), the encrypted backup — its key, file and what a restore adds (`backup.js`), when the screen lock locks (`app-lock.js`). No DOM access; covered by `tests/*.test.mjs` |
| `app/js/store.js` | App state and persistence (the private file, the shared files, the sync state and the settings as records of the vault, read at start into memory), moving notes between files, change events |
| `app/js/vault.js` | The encrypted local vault's platforms (backlog #19): the Android app's Vault plugin, IndexedDB `notedown-vault` on the web, memory in unit tests; takes over the plain data of older versions on first open (`docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Where the files live") |
| `app/js/platform.js` | Whether this is the Android app — or `?platform=android`, which simulates it in a browser — and the Android-only plugins with their stand-ins for the simulation |
| `app/js/sync/` | Real sync of the private file: the server API (`api.js`), the device keys in IndexedDB and every other secret in the vault (`keystore.js`), turning on, linking by QR code or with the recovery key, sync rounds, removing a device and signing out with a local erase, ending sync when the identity was deleted (`client.js`); deleting the identity with the recovery key (`delete-identity.js`); contacts: invitations, requests and their checks (`contacts.js`) |
| `app/js/sync-sim.js` | Prototype only: simulates the server for the sample (`?sample`) — sync status "syncing" → "synced" after each file change, offline |
| `app/config.json` | The sync server's address (`api`), the web app's (`web`, the start of invitation links), the `operator` the legal texts name, the `version` and the `source` repository Settings → About shows; empty in the repository, written by the web and Android deploys (`scripts/write-config.js`) from repository variables (`docs/operations.md`) |
| `app/privacy/`, `app/terms/`, `app/legal/` | The privacy policy and the terms of use, German and English (`docs/requirements.md` → "Legal texts and license"); `legal.js` fills in the operator from `app/config.json`, `?sample` shows placeholders |
| `app/licenses.json` | The third-party components of the web and Android app with version and license text, generated by `scripts/make-licenses.js` for Settings → About |
| `app/import/` | The Google Keep import page (`docs/requirements.md` → "Import from Google Keep"): reads a Takeout ZIP in the browser, previews the notes as cards with selection and imports the chosen ones into this browser's private file (`store.js` → `importNotes`); its DOM-free logic is `app/js/core/keep-import.js` and `app/js/core/zip.js`, `?sample` previews `app/sample/keep.json` |
| `app/admin/` | The server owner's admin page (`docs/requirements.md` → "Server maintenance (admin)"): overview, identities, storage limit per identity, blocking and deleting an identity, news posts, backup and restore; signs in with this browser's linked device through `app/js/sync/api.js`, its DOM-free logic and the `?sample` stand-in for the server are in `app/js/core/admin.js`, the sample server in `app/sample/admin.json` |
| `app/delete/` | The page that deletes an identity with its recovery key (`docs/requirements.md` → "Deleting your sync data"); no sign-in, the server as in the app (`?api=`, this browser's, `config.json`); the signing is `app/js/sync/delete-identity.js`, which Sync & sharing uses too; `?sample` deletes nothing |
| `app/invite/`, `app/js/invite-link.js` | Invitation links: the page a link opens forwards into the app, which opens Add contact for it (also the Android App Link, verified through `.well-known/assetlinks.json`, which the web deploy writes from the signing key) |
| `app/js/ui/` | Views: note list (`note-list.js`, also starts / ends editing), editor (`editor.js` + `live-preview.js`, CodeMirror), toolbar (`toolbar.js`), taps on counters — the pop-up with its steps, typed amount and stopwatch, the running time (`counter.js`), the running stopwatches above the list (`watch-bar.js`), the long-press menu of a task's states (`task-menu.js`), speech input (`dictation.js`), the + button with hold-to-record (`recorder.js`), multi-select with its action bar and order dialog (`selection.js`), the custom order's arrange dialog (`arrange.js`), table of contents with section selection and the phone sheet's handle (`toc.js`), swiping between notes and archive and between the contents panel's tabs (`view-swipe.js`), the trash's actions — restore, restore for its circle, delete permanently (`trash.js`), search hits highlighted in notes and contents with their counter and ▲ / ▼ (`search-hits.js`), the people overview that filters the list by circle (`people-list.js`), the Labels tab and the label filter (`labels.js`), verifying a contact by safety code or scan (`verify-contact.js`), menus, snackbar, the confirmation dialog (`confirm.js`), icons, date labels, the "Sync & sharing" panel (`sync-panel.js`, whose container also holds the share dialog `share-dialog.js`) with its QR code and camera scanner (`qr.js`), contact colors and avatars (`people.js`), the due-date reminders — settings page, permission, web timer, Android local notifications, the simulated banner (`reminders.js`), when a news post counts as seen (`news-seen.js`), the export dialog (`export.js`), links and embedded media by this device's setting with the "Open link?" dialog (`external.js`), the settings (`settings.js`, its About section reading the version and source address from `app/js/app-info.js`) with their Open-source licenses page (`licenses.js`), their Links & media page (`external-settings.js`; the Reminders page is in `reminders.js`), their Backup pages — create, the backup key, restore (`backup.js`), the screen lock with its settings page and the lock screen (`app-lock.js`), the version history pages in the Sync & sharing panel (`history.js`), the card above the notes when sync stopped on this device — removed, deleted, blocked, outdated — and, temporarily (backlog #20), the one asking for the recovery key once (`sync-notice.js`, its page `recovery-kem.js`), small DOM helpers and the history entries of the layers the Android back key closes (`dom.js`) |
| `app/js/main.js` | Wires store and views: top bar, sorting, search, keyboard, prototype options |
| `app/js/sample.js` | Prototype only: loads the sample notes and the sample identity (`?sample`) |
| `app/welcome.md` | The welcome notes a first start shows, one per `## ` heading (onboarding; the only note text outside `app/sample/`) |
| `app/sample/` | `notes.md`: the sample notes, in the real file format — the only source of example content (CLAUDE.md), with permanent notes and a trash (one note deleted by the others of a circle); `sharing.json`: the sample user, devices, contacts, which notes are shared with whom and which news posts the user has seen or closed; `news.md`: the server owner's sample news posts (the app's feed and the admin page's `?sample`); `admin.json`: the sample server the admin page shows with `?sample` (IDs and sizes, no note text); `media/`: the files behind the sample's embedded image and video, whose addresses look external (`sample.js` → `SAMPLE_MEDIA`); `dictation.md`: the transcript `?dictation=demo` replays; `keep.json`: a Google Keep export (the files of a Takeout ZIP) the import page's `?sample` previews, its texts taken from `notes.md` |
| `app/vendor/` | Third-party code, committed as files: `marked` (Markdown rendering), `codemirror.esm.js` (the editor; one bundle of the CodeMirror 6 packages listed in `scripts/vendor/`), `qrcode.esm.js` (qrcode-generator, draws QR codes), `jsqr.esm.js` (jsQR, decodes camera frames; Apache-2.0), `capacitor-core.esm.js` (`@capacitor/core`, reaches the Android app's native plugins), `mlkem.wasm` + `mlkem.js` (ML-KEM-768 from libcrux-ml-kem, Cryspen's formally verified Rust code as in libsignal, as WebAssembly without imports, and its hand-written loader; Apache-2.0), each with its license (the others MIT) |

Rules: plain HTML/CSS/JS as ES modules, no framework, no external
requests at runtime; third-party code only as a vendored file with its
license. The CodeMirror and jsQR bundles and the qrcode and Capacitor copies are generated
from the versions pinned in `scripts/vendor/`: to add an export or update
one, edit `scripts/vendor/*.entry.js` / `package.json` and run `npm install && npm run build` in `scripts/vendor/`
(only needed when changing it — the app itself never needs a build). `mlkem.wasm` is built from the crate in
`scripts/vendor/mlkem/` (libcrux-ml-kem pinned in `Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock`, the Rust toolchain in
`rust-toolchain.toml`) by its `build.sh`, which gives the same bytes on every run; then rerun `make-licenses.js`. New logic that doesn't touch the DOM goes into `app/js/core/`
with a unit test.

### Prototype options (variants)

Where a decision is still open, the prototype carries the variants side
by side: ⋮ → "Prototype: …" switches them, and URL parameters preset
them for screenshots and links. Once the user decides, the losing variant
is deleted from code, menu and this table.

| Parameter | Values | What it switches |
|---|---|---|
| `flavor` | `system` · `latte` · `frappe` · `macchiato` · `mocha` | Theme (a real setting, not a variant) |
| `view` | `closed` · `trash` | Start in the archive or the trash |
| `dictation` | `demo` | Replay `app/sample/dictation.md` instead of the microphone (not a variant) |
| `sample` | — | Replace the stored notes, shared files and sync state with the sample notes and the sample identity (not a variant; replaces real data) |
| `sync` | `off` | Like `sample`, but with sync off and no shared files, all sample notes private (not a variant) |
| `api` | URL | Use this sync server and remember it in this browser (local testing, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8765`; empty value forgets it; not a variant) |
| `platform` | `android` | Simulate the Android app in a browser: Settings → Privacy (screen lock, screen security, incognito keyboard) and the lock screen, with stand-ins for the native plugins (not a variant) |

In ⋮ → "Prototype", "Go offline" / "Go online" simulates losing the connection, "Simulate device removal" shows what a removed device sees (sync off, the card above the notes; reload with `?sample` to get the sample identity back), "Simulate outdated app" the card of an app the server no longer serves, and "Show storage hint again" brings back a hidden "only stored in this browser" card (not variants).

### Screenshots

```bash
NODE_PATH="$(npm root -g)" node scripts/screenshot.js --device phone --theme dark \
  --query "view=closed" --out <scratchpad>/shot-phone-dark.png \
  [--eval "<js that opens the state to show>"]
```

The script serves the repo itself, starts each run with empty storage
and the sample notes (`--first-start` shows the welcome notes instead),
lists page errors and exits non-zero on them. Options are documented in its header.

The README pictures live in `docs/images/` (desktop 1440 px wide, phone
shots scaled to 585 px); retake them with this script when the look of
the main list changes noticeably.

## Technology direction

Decided on 2026-10-13, once function and look stood:

- **Web code in a native shell (Capacitor)** for Android and iOS, the
  same code as a web app / PWA for the browser — the prototype's
  HTML/CSS/ES modules carry over as they are; native features (files,
  speech recognition, app shortcuts) come from Capacitor plugins.
  Obsidian's mobile app is built the same way. No build step for the web
  code; plugin modules are vendored like the other third-party files.
- **Android and web first**, iOS later (needs an Apple developer account
  and signing).
- **Milestone 1: sync between the user's own devices** (identity,
  recovery key, linking and removing devices, the private file);
  contacts and sharing follow in milestone 2. The UI for both stays in
  the prototype.
- **Editor:** CodeMirror 6, as in the prototype.
- **Speech:** the browser's Web Speech API on the web; on Android (whose
  web view has none) Android's `SpeechRecognizer` through the app's own
  Capacitor plugin (`DictationPlugin.java`, see "Android app") behind the
  same `startDictation` interface (`app/js/ui/dictation.js`) — the
  community plugin reports neither errors nor the input level.
- A UI framework, if any, is decided later; `app/js/core/` stays
  framework-free either way.
- **Backend:** Python with FastAPI, a stateless API
  (`docs/server-api.md`) with Postgres — for the test phase Postgres also
  holds the encrypted files; an object store comes when size calls for
  it. Encryption uses WebCrypto, which the browser and the Capacitor web
  view both offer, plus ML-KEM-768 as vendored WebAssembly (libcrux).
- **Hosting for the live test:** GitHub Pages (web app), Google Cloud
  Run (server), Neon (Postgres), APKs as a GitHub pre-release — free
  tiers, HTTPS on the owner's subdomains (`docs/operations.md`).

## Server

`server/` is a FastAPI app (`notedown_server/`) with pytest tests against
a real Postgres; `server/Dockerfile` is what Cloud Run runs.

```bash
scripts/test-server.sh      # venv + throwaway local Postgres, then pytest
```

It uses `TEST_DATABASE_URL` instead when set (an empty test database);
CI runs the same tests against a Postgres service. Run them when
`server/` changed. When the sync client (`app/js/sync/`, `crypto.js`,
`merge.js`) or the server changed, also run the end-to-end test, which
drives several browser "devices" against a local server:

```bash
scripts/test-sync.sh [--shots <dir>]   # screenshots of the sync pages
``` `protocol.py` holds the encodings
and device-list rules without I/O, `auth.py` challenges and tokens,
`app.py` the endpoints, `schema.sql` the tables (applied at start, only
additive statements).

## Android app

`mobile/` holds the Capacitor configuration (`webDir` is `../app`) and
the generated Android project in `mobile/android/`; the copied web files
are not committed. Native code of our own sits next to `MainActivity.java`,
which registers it: `DictationPlugin.java` (speech input),
`ShareFilePlugin.java` (hands an export or a backup to the share sheet; the plain export's copy in the cache goes at the next start),
`VaultPlugin.java` (the encrypted vault's files in `files/vault/` and its data key, sealed by the Android Keystore — `docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Where the files live"),
`PrivacyPlugin.java` (screen security, the incognito keyboard and the screen lock through `androidx.biometric` — `docs/requirements.md` → "Privacy on the device") with `SecureWebView.java`, Capacitor's web view with the incognito keyboard, put in place by `res/layout/capacitor_bridge_layout_main.xml`. `AndroidManifest.xml` keeps the app out of every system backup (`allowBackup="false"`, `res/xml/backup_rules.xml`, `res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml`). The app's
static pages are linked as `<page>/index.html`: Capacitor's local server
answers a path without a file name (`privacy/`) with the app's own page. Community plugins are npm dependencies in `mobile/package.json` (`@capacitor/local-notifications` for the due-date reminders) and reached from `app/` through the vendored `@capacitor/core` (`registerPlugin`), so no further JS is vendored. The launcher
icon (adaptive: Mauve background, foreground and monochrome layer) and the
splash screen (androidx core-splashscreen: the icon on `splash_background`,
Latte base / Mocha base in `values-night`) are ours, not Capacitor's
defaults; their PNGs come from `scripts/make-icons.js`. The APK is built by CI (`.github/workflows/android.yml`);
locally it needs Node, JDK 21 and the Android SDK:

```bash
cd mobile && npm ci && npx cap sync android
cd android && ./gradlew assembleDebug
```
